method.policy: Multi-source corroboration required; political control is separated from route, fortress, settlement and commercial presence.
method.dateGuard: Do not back-project post-1326 Eretna, Sutayli, Aq Qoyunlu or later Turkoman territorial arrangements into 1326.

anchors.name: Sivas
anchors.evidence: 1326 falls inside Timurtash's 1318–1327 Anatolian governorship; Eretna's later autonomous polity is not promoted to 1326.

anchors.name: Erzincan
anchors.evidence: Independent academic work describes taxation and coinage under Ilkhanid rule through 1243–1343; Kemah/Erzincan corridor functioned as an east-west route.

anchors.name: Kemah
anchors.controlModel: fortress and route anchor within the Erzincan/Firat corridor
anchors.evidence: TDV identifies Kemah as a strategically positioned medieval fortress on the Karasu/Firat valley; exact 1326 territorial polygon remains unproven.

anchors.name: Erzurum
anchors.evidence: Academic study of the Ilkhanid period describes Erzurum as an important Ilkhanid trade centre; 1326 travel evidence is also reported in secondary scholarship.

anchors.name: Bayburt
anchors.evidence: TDV traces Bayburt's Seljuk and Ilkhanid development and its strategic fortification against Trabzon; later Eretna control is post-1334 and excluded.

anchors.name: Ispir
anchors.evidence: Cambridge archaeological-historical study describes Ispir and Bayburt as long-term marcher territory between competing powers and highlights Ispir's control of the Coruh valley and route to the Black Sea.

anchors.name: Trabzon
anchors.evidence: TDV identifies Trabzon as the capital of the Komnenian empire, with Ilkhanid overlordship in the period and Genoese/Venetian commercial colonies; Türkmen pressure intensified from the 1320s, especially in surrounding western/southern mountains.

anchors.name: Giresun
anchors.controlModel: Trebizond sphere with frontier pressure; exact 1326 control needs local reconstruction
anchors.evidence: TDV records 1297 Turkish advances, early-14th-century attacks and 1301 refortification by Alexios II; this supports a contested frontier model rather than a smooth later boundary.

negativeControls.name: Eretna State
negativeControls.reason: Eretna's independent polity belongs to the post-1327/post-1335 political transformation.

negativeControls.name: Aq Qoyunlu
negativeControls.reason: TDV places their emergence in this regional political theatre from 1340 onward.

negativeControls.name: Sutayli/late Ilkhanid successor polities
negativeControls.reason: Their regional dominance belongs to the post-1335 fragmentation period.

modelingRules: Do not draw a single hard Ilkhanid–Trebizond border across the Pontic mountains without local evidence.
Treat fortress nodes and mountain passes independently from province ownership.
Separate imperial suzerainty from direct local administration.
Treat Trabzon's Genoese/Venetian commercial presence as a trade-network layer, not foreign sovereignty.
Use post-1326 events only as chronology brackets, never as direct 1326 ownership evidence.
